package_info.package_versions: All Python versions supporting sitecustomize/usercustomize modules (e.g., Python 3.x)
package_info.why_malicious: This technique exploits Python's automatic import of usercustomize.py and sitecustomize.py from site-packages directories to achieve persistent, stealthy code execution on every Python interpreter invocation. By placing arbitrary code in these files, attackers can ensure their payload runs repeatedly, acting as a backdoor and persistence mechanism without user awareness or consent.

required_permissions: filesystem (write access to user site-packages directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print("[!] Malware could have run here")
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code executes a print statement (as a placeholder for arbitrary Python code), runs automatically on every Python interpreter startup, and can access user data or perform malicious actions, resulting in persistent execution of attacker-controlled logic.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Any code placed in usercustomize.py is executed automatically by the Python interpreter on every startup, regardless of which script is run. Attackers can exploit this to persistently execute malicious code without user knowledge, enabling stealthy backdoors or data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Python packages should not execute arbitrary code on every interpreter invocation outside of explicit user intent. This behavior subverts user expectations and standard package operation by introducing hidden, persistent execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use includes customizing the Python environment for user-specific needs, such as modifying sys.path or setting environment variables, but not for persistent, hidden, or unauthorized code execution.
key_indicators: Presence of usercustomize.py in user site-packages directory
Automatic execution of code on every Python interpreter start
Recent or unexpected modification of usercustomize.py
Potential for arbitrary code execution without explicit user action

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: print("[!] Malware could have run here")
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code executes a print statement (as a placeholder for arbitrary Python code), runs automatically on every Python interpreter startup in the global or virtual environment, and can access environment-wide data or perform malicious actions, resulting in persistent execution of attacker-controlled logic across all Python sessions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: sitecustomize.py is loaded automatically by the Python interpreter from global or virtualenv site-packages, allowing attackers to persistently execute code across all Python invocations in that environment. This enables environment-wide persistence and potential compromise of all Python-based processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not inject persistent code into sitecustomize.py to run on every interpreter start. This is a clear abuse of the customization mechanism, which is intended for legitimate environment-wide configuration, not for hidden or malicious persistence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use includes environment-wide configuration or setup, such as setting up logging or environment variables, but not for hidden, persistent, or unauthorized code execution.
key_indicators: Presence of sitecustomize.py in global or virtualenv site-packages directory
Automatic execution of code on every Python interpreter start
Recent or unexpected modification of sitecustomize.py
Potential for arbitrary code execution without explicit user action

attack_chain.action: Attacker writes malicious code to usercustomize.py in the user's site-packages directory or sitecustomize.py in the global/virtualenv site-packages directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistent execution of malicious code on every Python interpreter invocation.

attack_chain.action: Every time the Python interpreter is started, the malicious code in usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py is automatically executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor/persistence: attacker code runs repeatedly, can exfiltrate data or perform other malicious actions.

behavioral_signatures: Automatic execution of code from usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py on every Python interpreter start
Unexpected or unauthorized modification of usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py files
Persistence of code execution across all Python scripts and sessions
Presence of non-standard or suspicious code in usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py, especially code that initiates network connections or accesses sensitive data
file_indicators: Presence of usercustomize.py in user site-packages directory (e.g., ~/.local/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages/usercustomize.py)
Presence of sitecustomize.py in global or virtualenv site-packages directory (e.g., /venv/lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages/sitecustomize.py)
Recent modification timestamps on usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py
Unexpected file size or content changes in these files
network_indicators: Any network activity (e.g., HTTP requests, DNS lookups) initiated from usercustomize.py or sitecustomize.py
Unexpected outbound connections from Python processes immediately upon interpreter startup
Connections to suspicious or unrecognized domains or IPs from Python processes at startup
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the creation or modification of usercustomize.py and sitecustomize.py files in all site-packages directories. Use file integrity monitoring to alert on changes or unexpected content. Flag any non-standard or unauthorized code in these files, especially if it initiates network connections or accesses sensitive data. Review Python interpreter startup logs for unexpected output or behavior. Restrict write permissions to site-packages directories where possible. In sensitive environments, use interpreter options (-S, -s, or PYTHONNOUSERSITE) to disable automatic imports of these files.
